title: The Mage
timelinePosition: Opens on the exact beat where Chapter 1 ends; Jaina has been in detention for hours (roughly eight hours since her last resonance reading).
openLocation: Farstrider border post at Thalassian Pass, inside the containment ward circle
transport: On foot inside the ward circle at open; southbound on Thalassian horses once Sylvanas lets her out.
immediateObjective: Get Sylvanas to act on the contamination before more time is lost.
constraints: Absolute limited third on Jaina; no head-hopping, nothing she could not perceive or infer
Do not replay Chapter 1's closing line 'Start talking'; Beat 1 opens from Sylvanas's order already given
Jaina does not know Sylvanas felt a stone read wrong or saw it circled on the map
No confirmation that grain is the carrier; do not name grain, bread or flour as cause
No trust and no warmth between Jaina and Sylvanas; grim working alignment only
Jaina's first read of Sylvanas as cold military obstruction breaks at Beat 9 and not earlier
Cyndia in pre-Ch10 voice: crisp, professional, volunteers field observations
The unnamed fourth ranger is background only; no continuity built around her
Lyriel does not use Jaina's first name in this chapter; she is the only ranger who talks to Jaina and jokes
Neral is a relay rider and strong rider; she appears only in Ch 2-3

povKnowsAtOpen: The leylines south of the border are contaminated by something necromantic
She can identify the signature as broadly death-aligned even though the banned discipline sits outside her formal training
She crossed into Quel'Thalas tracking the corruption
The Kirin Tor did not authorize the trip and Antonidas does not know exactly where she is
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: Whether Sylvanas already knows who she is
Whether the elves will release her or keep her prisoner
What the contamination is doing to the physical ground beyond the leylines
The exact process that turns living contamination into post-death behavior
mustNotBeImpliedYet: Immediate trust between Jaina and Sylvanas
Proof of an organized cult network
Anything warmer than a grim, working alignment
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Sylvanas is convinced enough to release Jaina and ride south with her
The contamination is physical, lethal and large enough to threaten the whole region, active in living flesh before death
The riding party is Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia, Lyriel, Neral and one unnamed escort ranger, heading to Millhaven
The entry method for the sickness is still unknown
Lyriel is the ranger who talks to Jaina on the road

pov: She opens convinced that if she can explain the magic clearly enough, any sensible person will act.
She starts out treating Sylvanas as another soldier standing in her way.
Because she assumes soldiers need the short version, she talks smaller than she really thinks.
By the end, Jaina still hates being under guard, but she stops treating Sylvanas like a blunt instrument and starts seeing how much she needs her on the road.

beats: Jaina first reads Sylvanas as a cold military obstruction: dangerous, precise, and mostly interested in custody.
That read breaks when Sylvanas listens fast, reads the map sharply, and handles the road like someone who actually knows what matters.
Once Sylvanas proves she can follow the problem, Jaina drops the watered-down explanation.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They start as prisoner and custodian. If Jaina gets out, it will be on a leash.
As the chapter moves, the custody arrangement turns into a working investigation.
There is still no trust and no warmth. They are only starting to become useful to each other.

castAndHandoffRules: Sylvanas Windrunner: leads the ride south once she decides to test Jaina's claim.
Ranger Cyndia: border-post officer who becomes the active escort lead.
Ranger Lyriel: right-flank escort and best shot in the mounted detail; the one ranger who talks to Jaina on the road and jokes where Cyndia will not.
Ranger Neral: third named escort and strongest rider; relay rider if word must go back.
Unnamed fourth ranger: background escort only. Do not build continuity around her.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 3 opens with this same party approaching Millhaven; all three named escorts and the unnamed ranger present.

factsLocked: The full mounted group arrives at Millhaven together
Cyndia, Lyriel, Neral and the unnamed escort ranger are the active riding party alongside Sylvanas and Jaina
Lyriel is the ranger who talks to Jaina on the road
The contamination is confirmed physical, lethal and spreading
The entry method for the sickness is still unknown to them
factsNotEarned: Grain as the weapon and carrier

scenes.title: The Interrogation
scenes.sceneFunction: Jaina has to talk her way out of custody and into an escorted ride south.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Jaina knows the contamination is real. Sylvanas only knows she has a high-profile trespasser inside the wards (Chapter 1 close: she knows the name and has seen the circled stone on the map; Jaina knows neither). Jaina has been in the cell for hours and has not yet delivered her warning on the page.
scenes.arcPressure: Jaina's first read of Sylvanas as another soldier in her way: she shrinks the explanation to the short version and pays for it.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only (silvermoon-and-quelthalas.md): ward-stones carry warmth, bass vibration and old runes; border hum fades into human air at Thalassian Pass. Chapter 1 enrichment (warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Eversong, /Thalassian_Pass) carried over: Highborne runestones dampen non-elven magic, which is why Jaina feels suppressed in the holding circle. No new web research was run for this chapter; cell and anchor-stone mechanics are inferred from the outline and Chapter 1 plan, not sourced.

beats.goal: Get Sylvanas to hear the danger now, before more time is lost; drop diplomacy and open with the contamination itself.
beats.conflict: Every word is being weighed by a listener sharper than the officers who dismissed her; the ward suppresses her magic, she is exhausted, and she cannot tell whether she will be believed.

outcome.summary: Jaina throws the warning down hard and Sylvanas lets her keep going, but gives no sign of belief.

beats.goal: Make the case for corrupted leylines: tracked broadly necromantic damage until Thalassian ward-stones carried the same signature, then crossed the border to confirm.
beats.conflict: She trims the explanation for a soldier and sounds thinner than she is; her map and tools are confiscated, including the paired sending stone to Antonidas that she has kept silent so he cannot order her home; Cyndia listens motionless.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas skips the theory and goes for the practical weak point, why Jaina came alone.

beats.goal: Answer why she came alone without making herself sound reckless.
beats.conflict: The honest answer is the worst one: no Kirin Tor authorization, no credentials, no backing, only a note left on Antonidas's desk; nobody in Dalaran acted on her warning.

outcome.summary: The admission makes her look both reckless and honest, and Sylvanas reaches the point of deciding whether this is worth verifying.

beats.emotion: Jaina sees that argument will not get her out of the circle; the cost of the failed persuasion lands as tired clarity.
beats.dilemma: Keep arguing from inside the ward, or accept that only proof on the road will count.
beats.decision: She commits to proving the danger out of doors. Sylvanas asks which stones read worst and where, listens to that answer harder than anything else, and offers a conditional release.

beats.goal: Accept any terms that get her moving.
beats.conflict: Armed escort, watched hands, no wandering; her pride and her hours on the warded floor against the clock.

outcome.summary: She accepts at once and admits she needs the escort to survive the road; the ward drops and she feels the contamination is worse than she had measured.

scenes.title: The Road to Millhaven
scenes.sceneFunction: The warning comes off the page and starts showing itself in the land.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The contamination is urgent, but they still do not know how it enters the physical world. Jaina's read of Sylvanas is still 'cold military obstruction'. Lyriel's pre-Ch4 register: mock-solemn 'Lady Proudmoore', not yet 'Jaina'.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas proves she can follow the problem; Jaina drops the watered-down explanation and stops treating her as a blunt instrument.
scenes.enrichment: Thalassian horses (thalassian-horses.md): fine-boned, trained to ward-stone hum, sidestep then settle; light quiet tack, creak of leather, hot breath after a hard push. Plague mechanism (plague-mechanism.md): Jaina at Ch 2-3 sees necromancy, design, saturation, ingress and reanimation, but cannot split carrier, host change and death trigger; keep her never clueless, still incomplete. Millhaven geography is not in the project locations files; lordaeron-and-northrend.md was not consulted by this planner for road detail.

beats.emotion: The corrupted leyline signal hits Jaina at full strength the moment the ward network falls behind, a physical blow; the elven wards had been hiding the scale.
beats.dilemma: Trust the reading she has and push on, or test the road itself to learn whether the source is a place, an object or an ongoing event.
beats.decision: She decides to test the road physically.
newOnPageInformation: The ward network was masking the true scale of the corruption
Out here the pressure is far worse than she could prove from inside the post
The elves feel the shift only as tension in the ride
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the source is a place, an object or an ongoing event

beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: the decision to test the road is the next beat's physical act

beats.goal: Read the ground itself with a bare hand to learn how deep the corruption has gone.
beats.conflict: Reading deep makes her a liability in the open; the rangers must cover her kneeling form, and the reading costs her.

outcome.summary: She learns the wrongness has seeped out of the leylines into ground and water, taking root in living systems; Sylvanas notes the liability; Jaina remounts and misreads her audience again.

beats.decision: The party presses on toward the town limits; the dread turns violent out of nowhere.

scenes.title: The Wildlife Attack
scenes.sceneFunction: The plague turns physical and violent, and Jaina sees how Sylvanas handles a real fight.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The land is contaminated, but the living cost has not shown its teeth yet.
scenes.arcPressure: Jaina sees Sylvanas command a fight with no wasted words and then has to put her hand in the evidence while Sylvanas waits on her.
scenes.enrichment: Neral voice sheet: relay rider, strongest rider; she leaves in Ch 3 with the survivor girl and the dispatch. Lyriel voice sheet: truthful, jokes with a flat exaggerated comparison, combat calls are direction-target-action only. Wildlife behavior is invented per the outline; no canon source consulted.

beats.goal: Survive the ambush while Jaina casts on instinct.
beats.conflict: Sick wild-eyed deer burst from the trees, wolves hit the horses from the flank; the fight is too fast for planning; one deer keeps moving when it should be dead.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas commands with almost no wasted words and the escort does its part cleanly; the field is clear but Jaina must face what the theory means in flesh.

beats.plannerWarning: 'Keeps moving after it should be dead' is ambiguous against B12's active-before-death finding. Write it as wounded and still on its feet, not a reanimated corpse. No organized undead column.

beats.goal: Examine the carcasses to learn whether this is isolated or part of the spreading pattern.

outcome.summary: The necromantic agent is in tissue, blood and organs and active in living flesh before death; Sylvanas holds the company for the read, then they remount and push hard toward the strongest wrongness.
